bib.title: Medical Graph RAG: Towards Safe Medical Large Language Model via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

question: How can graph-based RAG be adapted to the medical domain so LLMs give evidence-based, source-traceable answers over private medical data?
hypothesis: Linking user documents to credible sources and controlled vocabularies (Triple Graph Construction) and retrieving by tag hierarchy (U-Retrieval) will beat standard RAG and GraphRAG.
contributions: First specialised framework for graph-based RAG in the medical domain (MedGraphRAG).
Triple Graph Construction and U-Retrieval enabling evidence-based responses using holistic RAG data.
Outperforms other retrieval methods and fine-tuned medical LLMs across a wide range of medical Q&A benchmarks, new SOTAs.
Human evaluation shows more understandable and evidence-based responses.

method.summary: Documents are chunked semantically by an LLM, entities (name, type from UMLS semantic types, context) are extracted, linked by embedding cosine similarity to a two-layer RepoGraph (medical books/papers, UMLS) to form [RAG entity, source, definition] triples, and relationships are generated, giving Meta-MedGraphs. Each graph gets predefined-tag summaries, clustered agglomeratively into a multi-layer tag hierarchy. U-Retrieval descends the tag hierarchy top-down to a target graph, answers from top-N entities and neighbours, then refines the answer bottom-up with higher-level tag summaries.
method.task: medical QA (multiple choice), health fact-checking, long-form citation-backed generation

models.name: Llama3-70B as graph construction LLM L_G

inference.samples: 5-shot response ensemble (Li et al. 2024, More agents is all you need); single run otherwise unstated; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: same query prompt for all models; graph prompt: 'Given QUESTION: {Q}. GRAPH: {...}. Answer the user question: QUESTION using the graph: GRAPH...'
inference.retrieval: U-Retrieval: 4 levels on GPT-4, 5 for others; top 60 entities with 16-hop neighbours; all thresholds 0.5 unless noted; text-embedding-3-large embeddings

parameters.delta_t (tag merge): dynamic, merges top 20% most similar pairs each iteration

other.tag categories: Symptoms, Patient History, Body Functions, Medication (most important)

eval.protocol: All retrieval methods use same RAG and test data. Human evaluation by 7 certified clinicians and 5 laypersons. No significance test or seeds reported.

limits: Only the future-work line concedes limits: real-time data updates and validation on real-world clinical data are not done.
RAG data is MIMIC-IV, a public dataset; no private clinical deployment tested.
Test sets are multiple-choice or fact-check; long-form quality is judged only on 50-question DiverseHealth plus MultiMedQA samples, rater scale and sample counts not given.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; 5-shot ensemble used for all models, and comparison with baselines on the same ensemble is stated but costs are not reported.
Decoding settings, temperature, prompts for chunking/entity/relationship steps are not given in the text.
Table 3 ablation does not name the LLM.
Cost claim (cheaper than GraphRAG communities) is asserted, no cost numbers.
Baselines are LangChain RAG and the Azure GraphRAG implementation, not tuned variants.

terms.definition: a graph fixed across users that provides established sources and controlled vocabulary definitions for user RAG documents, built in two layers (papers/books, UMLS)
linking user RAG entities to source entities (TheReferenceOf) and these to dictionary entities (definition of), yielding [RAG entity, source, definition]
a directed graph generated for each data chunk
top-down precise retrieval through a tag hierarchy followed by bottom-up response refinement
